name: RTKLIB
summary: The original open-source GNSS positioning package by T. Takasu: SPP, DGNSS, RTK, PPK and PPP engines in portable C, plus CLI tools (rnx2rtkp, rtkrcv, str2str, convbin) and Windows GUIs.
why_it_matters: The reference implementation most GNSS research and low-cost RTK work is built on; reading its rtkpos.c is the fastest way to understand RTK.
hackathon_notes: Use str2str to relay NTRIP/serial streams and rnx2rtkp for post-processing. Upstream is quiet since 2024; prefer the demo5 fork for current receivers.

name: RTKLIB demo5 (rtklibexplorer)
summary: Actively maintained RTKLIB fork tuned for low-cost receivers (especially u-blox), with many robustness fixes to ambiguity resolution, cycle-slip handling and receiver decoders.
why_it_matters: The practical default for RTK/PPK with cheap F9P-class hardware; well documented through the rtklibexplorer blog.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt Windows binaries and Linux builds are easy. Pair with a u-blox F9P and a free NTRIP caster for cm-level fixes in an afternoon.

name: rtklib-py
summary: Python port of the demo5 RTKLIB positioning core, currently focused on post-processed kinematic (PPK) solutions.
why_it_matters: Readable Python version of RTK math, good for teaching, prototyping new filters or swapping in ML components.
hackathon_notes: Slow compared to C RTKLIB and PPK only; last pushed 2023. Ideal for instrumenting or modifying the filter during a hackathon.

name: MatRTKLIB
summary: MATLAB wrapper exposing RTKLIB functions and data structures (observations, navigation data, solutions) as MATLAB objects.
why_it_matters: Lets MATLAB users script RTKLIB processing and analysis without writing C.
hackathon_notes: Requires MATLAB. Useful if the team already lives in MATLAB for analysis plots. Since January 2025 the backend is MALIB (the RTKLIB successor), not RTKLIB 2.4.3; pre-compiled mex files ship for Windows, Ubuntu and macOS.

name: GNSS-SDR
summary: Full software-defined GNSS receiver built on GNU Radio: acquisition, tracking, navigation message decoding and PVT for GPS, Galileo, GLONASS and BeiDou signals from SDR front-ends or IQ files, including Galileo OSNMA support.
why_it_matters: The most complete open receiver for experimenting with signal-level defenses (tracking monitors, authentication, interference) on real or simulated IQ.
hackathon_notes: Install from distro packages (apt install gnss-sdr) to skip a long build. Feed it GPS-SDR-SIM or recorded IQ files; works with HackRF/USRP/RTL-SDR front-ends.

name: PocketSDR
summary: Open hardware GNSS front-end plus a software receiver (Python and C) by the RTKLIB author, supporting a wide range of GNSS signals across L1/L2/L5/L6 bands.
why_it_matters: Cheap path to multi-band raw IF capture and a readable receiver implementation, ideal for signal-level research.
hackathon_notes: Software runs on recorded IF without the hardware; building the board is out of hackathon scope unless pre-built.

name: GNSS-SDRLIB
summary: Older open-source GNSS software receiver library in C with a GUI, supporting several front-ends and real-time RTKLIB output.
why_it_matters: Compact receiver codebase that is easier to read than GNSS-SDR; historically a common teaching receiver.
hackathon_notes: Not updated since 2015 (repo not formally archived). v2.0 only runs on 64-bit Windows (Visual Studio 2012 build). Use for reference only; prefer PocketSDR or GNSS-SDR for live work.

name: FGI-GSRx
summary: Multi-GNSS software receiver in MATLAB from the Finnish Geospatial Research Institute, with modular acquisition, tracking and navigation stages.
why_it_matters: MATLAB receiver suitable for quick algorithm swaps (e.g. new tracking or interference mitigation) with readable code.
hackathon_notes: Needs MATLAB and IQ files; slow but transparent.

name: SoftGNSS v3.0 (maintained copy)
summary: Maintained copy of the classic Borre/Akos SoftGNSS MATLAB GPS L1 receiver with updates for several sampler front-ends.
why_it_matters: The receiver code that accompanies the standard textbook on software GPS receivers; the canonical teaching codebase.
hackathon_notes: Good for learning acquisition and tracking loops on a sample data file.

name: SoftGNSS-python
summary: Python port of the SoftGNSS software-defined GPS receiver toolkit.
why_it_matters: Python version of the textbook receiver; easier for teams without MATLAB.
hackathon_notes: Not updated since 2023 and written for Python 2.7 (README system requirements; installation section says 'Coming soon'). Expect porting work before offline IQ experiments.

name: GPS L1 Direct Position Estimation module
summary: Plug-in module adding Direct Position Estimation (positioning directly in the correlation domain) to MATLAB two-step software receivers such as SoftGNSS.
why_it_matters: DPE is studied for robustness in weak-signal, multipath and interference conditions; this is one of few open implementations.
hackathon_notes: Research code; computationally heavy. Useful as a stretch comparison against conventional tracking.

name: laika
summary: Python GNSS processing library from comma.ai that fetches orbits, clocks and atmospheric corrections automatically and computes corrected pseudoranges and positions from raw measurements.
why_it_matters: Quickest way to go from raw pseudoranges to a corrected fix in Python; it powered openpilot's laikad GNSS localizer until that was removed in October 2023.
hackathon_notes: Install from a clone (`pip install .`); the PyPI 'laika' package is a 2018 0.0.1 stub. Correction downloads need internet, and NASA CDDIS needs an Earthdata login in a .netrc. Good backend for Android raw data experiments.

name: gnss_lib_py
summary: Modular Python library from Stanford NavLab for parsing, analyzing and visualizing GNSS data (Android logs, RINEX, NMEA, SP3/CLK) with baseline positioning algorithms and fault detection examples.
why_it_matters: Strong Python base for smartphone GNSS work and for prototyping integrity/fault detection.
hackathon_notes: pip install gnss-lib-py; tutorials load GSDC data directly. Very good fit for a 24h spoofing-detection or integrity notebook.

name: georinex
summary: Fast Python reader for RINEX 2/3/4 observation and navigation files (plain, gzip/Z/bz2/zip or Hatanaka-compressed) and SP3 orbits into xarray, with batch conversion to NetCDF4/HDF5.
why_it_matters: Makes RINEX data accessible in the scientific Python stack without writing parsers.
hackathon_notes: pip install georinex. Use it to load public CORS/IGS RINEX for analysis or ML features.

name: gnssanalysis
summary: Geoscience Australia Python module of utilities for reading and comparing GNSS products (SP3, CLK, SINEX, Ginan outputs) and computing differences/statistics.
why_it_matters: Companion tooling for evaluating precise orbit/clock products and PPP outputs.
hackathon_notes: Niche; useful if comparing PPP solutions or product quality.

name: PRIDE PPP-AR
summary: Wuhan University's open-source multi-GNSS precise point positioning package with ambiguity resolution, aimed at geodetic-grade post-processing.
why_it_matters: Free PPP-AR gives cm-level positions without a local base station, a key capability where RTK networks are unavailable.
hackathon_notes: Command-line build via install.sh on Linux and macOS, plus a Windows GUI version; needs precise products downloaded. Post-processing only, so plan for hours of data.

name: Ginan
summary: Geoscience Australia's GNSS analysis toolkit for precise orbit determination and real-time/post-processed PPP, producing and consuming correction products.
why_it_matters: Government-backed open PPP and product-generation engine; relevant for sovereign correction services.
hackathon_notes: Heavy build and configuration; Docker images help. Overkill for most 48h builds.

name: GNSSTk
summary: C++ library (successor to GPSTk) from UT Austin ARL for GNSS data formats, time systems, ephemeris handling and positioning algorithms, with Python bindings.
why_it_matters: Long-lived, carefully engineered GNSS core library used in US research and monitoring work.
hackathon_notes: Build is CMake-heavy; use for robust format and time handling rather than quick demos.

name: pyubx2
summary: Python library for parsing and generating u-blox UBX protocol messages, including configuration (CFG-VALSET) and raw measurement (RXM-RAWX) messages.
why_it_matters: Standard way to talk to u-blox receivers from Python: configure, log raw data and read jamming/spoofing status fields (MON-HW, NAV-STATUS).
hackathon_notes: pip install pyubx2. Read MON-RF jamming indicators and NAV-STATUS spoof flags to build a live interference monitor quickly.

name: pyrtcm
summary: Python parser for RTCM 3 messages (MSM observations, station info, ephemerides, SSR).
why_it_matters: Lets teams inspect and manipulate correction streams from NTRIP casters in Python.
hackathon_notes: pip install pyrtcm. Combine with pygnssutils' NTRIP client for live streams.

name: pynmeagps
summary: Python library for parsing and generating NMEA 0183 GNSS sentences, including proprietary variants.
why_it_matters: NMEA is what most autopilots and COTS receivers emit; this is a well-maintained parser/generator.
hackathon_notes: pip install pynmeagps. Can also generate NMEA to feed test positions into a downstream system.

name: PyGPSClient
summary: Cross-platform Python GUI GNSS client that displays and configures receivers over NMEA, UBX, RTCM3 and other protocols, with built-in NTRIP and SPARTN clients.
why_it_matters: Fast visual tool for checking receiver state, satellite C/N0 and corrections during field tests.
hackathon_notes: pip install pygpsclient. Good bench tool to watch C/N0 drop during a jamming test in a shielded setup.

name: pygnssutils
summary: Python CLI and library utilities for reading, parsing and broadcasting GNSS streams, including an NTRIP client and caster/server and a socket server.
why_it_matters: Glue for building correction pipelines and logging tools without writing protocol code.
hackathon_notes: pip install pygnssutils; gnssntripclient gets you RTCM from a caster in one command.

name: pynmea2
summary: Lightweight Python library for parsing NMEA 0183 sentences.
why_it_matters: Widely used minimal NMEA parser.
hackathon_notes: pip install pynmea2; simpler than pynmeagps but less coverage.

name: gpsd
summary: Service daemon that monitors GNSS receivers over serial/USB/network and serves decoded fixes, satellites and timing to client applications via JSON over TCP.
why_it_matters: The standard Linux GNSS middleware; used for timing (with ntpd/chrony and PPS) and for multiplexing receivers to multiple apps.
hackathon_notes: apt install gpsd gpsd-clients; cgps/gpsmon give instant status. Use it for PPS timing demos.

name: ublox ROS driver
summary: ROS driver for u-blox receivers that publishes fixes, raw measurements and receiver status as ROS messages.
why_it_matters: Common bridge from u-blox hardware into ROS-based autonomy stacks.
hackathon_notes: Available as a ROS package; check the branch for ROS 1 vs ROS 2.

name: SparkFun u-blox GNSS v3 Arduino library
summary: Arduino library for u-blox GNSS modules over I2C/SPI/serial, covering configuration, high-precision fixes and RTK correction input.
why_it_matters: Easiest embedded route to an RTK-capable microcontroller node (ESP32 + F9P).
hackathon_notes: Many examples, including NTRIP over Wi-Fi on ESP32. Good for a low-cost rover or base station.

name: ubxlib
summary: u-blox's portable C libraries for building applications on their GNSS and cellular modules across MCU platforms.
why_it_matters: Vendor-maintained abstraction for u-blox hardware on embedded targets.
hackathon_notes: Repository is archived; prefer the SparkFun library or pyubx2.

name: ntripcaster (BKG standard caster)
summary: Maintained mirror of the BKG standard NTRIP broadcaster in C for distributing RTCM correction streams over HTTP.
why_it_matters: Self-hosted correction distribution for a private RTK network, e.g. in a contested area without public casters.
hackathon_notes: Builds with autotools; pair with str2str from RTKLIB as the source.

name: ntripcaster Docker
summary: Dockerfile and instructions to build and run the BKG NTRIP caster in a container.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to stand up your own caster.
hackathon_notes: docker build and go; last updated 2024.

name: go-gnss/ntrip
summary: Go library implementing NTRIP client, server and caster components.
why_it_matters: Modern, embeddable NTRIP implementation for building custom correction services.
hackathon_notes: Use as a library inside a Go backend; smaller community than BKG caster.

name: ROS NTRIP client
summary: ROS/ROS 2 node that connects to an NTRIP caster and publishes RTCM corrections, forwarding NMEA position back to the caster.
why_it_matters: Standard glue to get RTK corrections into a ROS robot.
hackathon_notes: apt-installable ROS package; works with any receiver driver accepting RTCM topics.

name: ntripbrowser
summary: Command-line tool that fetches and displays an NTRIP caster's source table, optionally filtered by distance from a coordinate.
why_it_matters: Quick way to find the nearest public base station mountpoint.
hackathon_notes: Needs libcurl. pip install ntripbrowser still installs the 2021 release (2.2.3); the repo is at 4.0.0 (2025, Python 3.11+), so install from a clone with make install for current code. Point at rtk2go or a national caster.

name: Node-NTRIP caster
summary: TypeScript/Node.js NTRIP caster library supporting NTRIP v1 and v2.
why_it_matters: JS option for web-stack teams building a correction relay.
hackathon_notes: Last updated 2023; fine for demos.

name: GPS Measurement Tools (incl. GnssLogger)
summary: Google's Android raw GNSS measurement tooling: the GnssLogger app source, MATLAB analysis tools for pseudorange processing (including a RINEX nav reader), and NMEA utilities.
why_it_matters: The canonical way to capture raw pseudoranges and carrier phase from phones, the basis for smartphone spoofing and integrity research.
hackathon_notes: Install GnssLogger from the Play Store and log on any recent Android phone; parse logs with gnss_lib_py.

name: GSDC 2023 solution (taroz)
summary: Code reproducing Taro Suzuki's Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge 2023 entry (1st on the public leaderboard, 2nd on the private one), using factor graph optimization of smartphone GNSS and IMU in MATLAB.
why_it_matters: Shows what state-of-the-art smartphone positioning looks like on a public benchmark.
hackathon_notes: Needs MATLAB and the Kaggle dataset; use as a baseline to compare against.

name: GPS-SDR-SIM
summary: Generates GPS L1 C/A baseband IQ sample files for a user-defined static or moving trajectory from a broadcast ephemeris file, for playback through an SDR.
why_it_matters: The standard open test-signal generator for evaluating receiver behavior under simulated or spoofed conditions. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.
hackathon_notes: Generate IQ files and feed GNSS-SDR directly (no RF needed) to test detectors. Repository archived in 2025 but still works. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

name: bladeGPS
summary: Real-time GPS L1 signal simulator variant of GPS-SDR-SIM for bladeRF hardware.
why_it_matters: Real-time variant for interactive receiver testing. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.
hackathon_notes: Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

name: LimeGPS
summary: Real-time GPS L1 signal simulator variant for LimeSDR.
why_it_matters: Same as bladeGPS for LimeSDR users. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.
hackathon_notes: Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

name: multi-sdr-gps-sim
summary: Maintained derivative of GPS-SDR-SIM that streams GPS L1 baseband on the fly to HackRF or ADALM-Pluto, or to a binary IQ file, with a curses text UI.
why_it_matters: More current option than the archived original for building test rigs. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.
hackathon_notes: Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

name: OSNMA-SDR-SIM
summary: Galileo E1-B/E5b signal simulator with OSNMA authentication data embedded, configurable OSNMA parameters and USRP or file output, tested against GNSS-SDR and OSNMAlib.
why_it_matters: Rare open tool to generate authenticated (and deliberately broken) Galileo signals for testing OSNMA-aware receivers.
hackathon_notes: Use file sink output into GNSS-SDR plus OSNMAlib for a full authenticate-or-alarm pipeline without RF. Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

name: Beidou-SDR-SIM
summary: Open-source generator for BeiDou B1C baseband signals for SDR playback or file output.
why_it_matters: Extends signal simulation testing beyond GPS to BeiDou.
hackathon_notes: Cabled or shielded-enclosure use only: radiating GNSS signals over the air is illegal in most jurisdictions.

name: OSNMAlib
summary: Python implementation of the Galileo OSNMA receiver protocol: verifies TESLA key chains and MACs on navigation data from several input formats (u-blox, Septentrio, GNSS-SDR, files).
why_it_matters: Most practical open tool to add navigation message authentication to a Galileo-capable receiver pipeline.
hackathon_notes: Works live with a u-blox receiver outputting SFRBX; needs the public key and Merkle root from the GSC. Good basis for an 'authenticated position' demo.

name: galileo-osnma (Rust)
summary: Rust implementation of Galileo OSNMA that can run on embedded no_std targets, with examples for live receivers.
why_it_matters: Lightweight, memory-safe OSNMA verifier suitable for embedding in drones or edge devices.
hackathon_notes: Cargo build; includes a u-blox-based example. Embedded angle is a differentiator.

name: FGI-OSNMA
summary: Python OSNMA implementation from the Finnish Geospatial Research Institute designed for flexibility and integration with receivers.
why_it_matters: Second independent Python OSNMA implementation for cross-checking.
hackathon_notes: Not updated since 2023; check against current ICD version.

name: OSNMA_ublox
summary: Jupyter-based real-time OSNMA authentication of u-blox receiver data in Python.
why_it_matters: Small, readable OSNMA example from the test phase.
hackathon_notes: Inactive since 2022, predates OSNMA public service; use for learning only.

name: galmon
summary: Open-source GNSS monitoring network and software that collects navigation data from volunteer receivers worldwide and publishes live health, ephemeris and timing statistics for Galileo, GPS, BeiDou and GLONASS.
why_it_matters: Independent constellation monitoring, valuable for spotting anomalies and checking broadcast data integrity.
hackathon_notes: Run a feeder with a u-blox receiver, or just consume the public galmon.eu data.

name: GPSSpy
summary: Python implementation of GPS jamming detection from receiver signal-to-noise ratio, following a published real-time jamming detection method.
why_it_matters: Simple, explainable C/N0-based jamming detector to start from.
hackathon_notes: Small codebase from 2021; adapt to read C/N0 from pyubx2 or Android logs.

name: Multi-frequency GNSS spoofing raw dataset
summary: Raw GNSS measurement logs from Android phones and smartwatches recorded under spoofing scenarios on L1, L5 and dual-band.
why_it_matters: Labelled smartphone spoofing data is scarce; this enables training and testing detectors without generating signals.
hackathon_notes: Load logs with gnss_lib_py and build a consistency-check or ML detector. Verify labelling and scenario details in the README before trusting results.

name: MAAST for ARAIM
summary: Stanford GPS Lab MATLAB toolset that evaluates Advanced RAIM availability and protection levels over service areas.
why_it_matters: Reference-grade integrity tooling from the lab behind much ARAIM research.
hackathon_notes: MATLAB; heavy on aviation integrity concepts. Use for coverage maps of integrity availability.

name: RAIM (MATLAB)
summary: MATLAB implementation of classic receiver autonomous integrity monitoring (fault detection and exclusion) for GNSS positioning.
why_it_matters: Compact RAIM example to adapt for spoofing/fault detection logic.
hackathon_notes: Small and readable; port the residual test to Python for a quick FDE demo.

name: gtsam_gnss
summary: Custom GTSAM factors and MATLAB wrappers for GNSS factor-graph positioning, including pseudorange, Doppler and carrier-phase factors with ambiguity estimation.
why_it_matters: Factor graphs are a robust way to fuse GNSS with other sensors and reject outliers.
hackathon_notes: Requires the author's GTSAM fork and MATLAB; under active development.

name: GraphGNSSLib
summary: Open-source GNSS positioning and RTK package using factor graph optimization, built on RTKLIB data handling and ROS.
why_it_matters: Shows FGO-based GNSS positioning outperforming filters in urban canyons; good research baseline.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 era code (last push 2022); expect build friction.

name: gnss_comm
summary: C++/ROS definitions and utilities for raw GNSS measurement processing (ephemeris, satellite positions, pseudorange models) used by GVINS.
why_it_matters: Reusable raw GNSS building blocks for tightly coupled GNSS-visual-inertial fusion.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; stable but unmaintained since 2022.

name: UT Starlink signal simulator
summary: MATLAB utility functions from UT Austin's Radionavigation Lab for simulating Starlink Ku-band downlink signals (OFDM frames, PSS/SSS, Doppler and path-loss histories), with MATLAB live-script playground examples.
why_it_matters: Lets teams experiment with Starlink as a signal of opportunity for PNT without capturing real Ku-band data.
hackathon_notes: Small MATLAB codebase, MIT licensed, last commit January 2024 and marked work in progress. The companion paper is Komodromos, Qin and Humphreys, 'Signal Simulator for Starlink Ku-Band Downlink' (ION GNSS+ 2023).

name: Starlink LEO-PNT
summary: Python project for passive positioning from Starlink downlink signals: TDOA/Doppler solvers, EKF, clock estimation and SDR capture tooling, with a dashboard.
why_it_matters: Recent hobbyist/research attempt at LEO signals-of-opportunity positioning end to end.
hackathon_notes: Single-author 2026 project; claims are unverified. Use as scaffolding, validate results yourself.

name: RINEX LEO extension proposal
summary: Proposal for RINEX format modifications to carry LEO-PNT observables and ephemeris.
why_it_matters: Shows how LEO-PNT data might be standardized into existing GNSS tooling.
hackathon_notes: Archived; read-only reference.

name: GNSS-Radar
summary: Web application showing current GNSS satellite positions (sky plot) for a location and time across constellations.
why_it_matters: Quick visibility planning tool for field tests.
hackathon_notes: Use the hosted site or run locally for offline sky plots.

name: openpilot
summary: Open driver-assistance robotics stack. Its current locationd fuses IMU and camera odometry in a pose Kalman filter; GNSS is still read and logged (ubloxd, qcomgpsd) but the laika-based GNSS fusion has been removed.
why_it_matters: Real-world example of a production fusion pipeline on consumer hardware, and of a stack that dropped GNSS from its localizer in favour of vision and IMU.
hackathon_notes: Large codebase; study locationd (pose_kf) and the ubloxd GNSS parsing rather than running the full stack. For laika-style GNSS processing, look at the standalone commaai/laika repo or older openpilot releases.
